#>     \code{n[i]} indices in that dimension, while a negative value
#>     excludes the last/first \code{abs(n[i])}, including all remaining
#>     indices. \code{NA} or non-specified values (when \code{length(n) <
#>       length(dim(x))}) select all indices in that dimension. Must
#>     contain at least one non-missing value.}
#>   }}
#> }
#> \value{
#> A data frame with the overdue rows.
#> }
#> \description{
#> Overdue rate
#> }
#> \section{Loan period}{
#>
#> A loan is overdue after 21 days.
#> }
#>
#> \seealso{
#> \code{\link[=overdue]{overdue()}}
#>
#> Other loan analyses:
#> \code{\link[=overdue]{overdue()}}
#> }
#> \concept{loan analyses}
rd("format_loan.Rd")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/loans.R
#> \name{format_loan}
#> \alias{format_loan}
#> \alias{print_loan}
#> \title{Format a loan}
#> \usage{
#> format_loan(x)
#>
#> print_loan(x)
#> }
#> \arguments{
#> \item{x}{A loan.}
#> }
#> \description{
#> Format a loan
#> }
#> \section{Functions}{
#> \itemize{
#> \item \code{print_loan()}: Print a formatted loan.
#>
#> }}
# An internal page keeps its topic but is left out of the indices.
squish <- readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "squish_loan.Rd"))
grep("^.(name|alias|keyword)", squish, value = TRUE)
#> [1] "\\name{squish_loan}"  "\\alias{squish_loan}" "\\keyword{internal}"

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Reuse documentation

overdue_rate() documents only by; the other three arguments came from overdue(). The ... was documented from utils::head() (the tag @inheritDotParams utils::head n names the one argument wanted) and the generated text says "Arguments passed on to" the function; the section "Loan period" and the value came over with @inheritSection and @inherit overdue returns. @family loan analyses on both blocks added "Other loan analyses:" to See Also on both pages, each linking to the other, and a \concept with the family name. @aliases overdue_ratio added an alias to the page, so help("overdue_ratio") finds it. @describeIn merged print_loan() into the page of format_loan() and described it in a "Functions" section; the roxygen2 documentation (and the 7.3.0 release) suggest @rdname, which gives the merged functions equal status and the usage of each, and is what shelf uses for book(), new_book() and validate_book(). The page for the internal helper was written but keeps only the internal keyword and no concept, so it is left out of the index of topics, and @noRd wrote no file at all (there are four Rd files for six blocks).

Three behaviours to know. @inheritParams copies only the arguments that the function has and does not document itself, and since roxygen2 8.0.0 it can be given the names of the arguments to take or to leave out (@inheritParams foo x y and @inheritParams foo -z). The source can be a function in another package (@inheritParams stats::lm), which needs that package to be installed when the documentation is generated. And @family needs the pages to exist in the same package: the "Other …​" list is made of the pages with the same family.

Links, topics and aliases

The markdown forms above are the usual way to link. For a topic in the same package [book()] links the alias book; for another package [pkg::fun()] writes a link with that package as an anchor, and the package should be listed in Imports or Suggests of DESCRIPTION, because the check for cross-references needs it ("Always list the linked package as a dependency", in the roxygen2 message that the first run of document() printed). Since roxygen2 8.0.0 all generated links share one code path, links to external packages use the topic alias as the anchor (which removed the R CMD check note about non-topic package-anchored links), and infix operators such as [%in%] can be linked. A link to a class is [Book-class] for S4, [book] for S3 (when the page’s alias is the class name), and [Book] for S7. The alias lists of the shelf pages show that one page often serves several topics; help.search() finds them by title, alias, concept and keyword.

Namespace tags

The same comments write the NAMESPACE. @export is the one every package uses, and its meaning depends on what it is on: a function gives export(name), an S3 method gives S3method(generic,class), an S4 class gives exportClasses(). The rule for S3 methods is strict: always export them, even when the generic is internal, since exporting is what registers the method; a method that is not exported is not found by dispatch in the installed package, although devtools::load_all() hides that mistake by exposing every function. roxygen2 warns about a method without a tag, as the "Messages" section below shows, and @exportS3Method NULL silences the warning for a method that is registered another way. For a method of a generic that lives in another package there are two ways: import the generic with @importFrom pkg generic and @export the method, or write @exportS3Method pkg::generic, which registers the method when the other package is loaded and needs no import. The shelf NAMESPACE, written by roxygen2 from the tags on format.book(), print.book(), summary.book() and print.summary.book() and on the ten exported functions, is this file:

# Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand

S3method(format,book)
S3method(print,book)
S3method(print,summary.book)
S3method(summary,book)
export(book)
export(clean_books)
export(clean_loans)
export(is_valid_isbn13)
export(loan_summary)
export(loans_per_month)
export(new_book)
export(normalise_isbn)
export(overdue_loans)
export(validate_book)

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Managing imports and exports

The first line is the roxygen2 header, then the S3 methods and then the functions, in alphabetical order. The directives are explained in Packages, Libraries and Namespaces; the point here is that no one edits this file: change a tag and run devtools::document(). A package that imports a function writes @importFrom pkg fun in the block of the function that uses it (or once in a package-level file), and roxygen2 8.1.1 writes the double-quoted form for non-syntactic names such as model<- to work around a base R bug in importFrom() directives.

Other tags: files, templates and generated Rd

A package whose files must be sourced in a given order (S4 classes that extend classes defined in other files) writes @include a-base.R and roxygen2 sets the Collate field of DESCRIPTION. A section shared by many pages can be written once in a file in man-roxygen/ and inserted with @template and @templateVar, although the reference says templates are superseded by inline R code. @evalRd runs R code and inserts the Rd it returns, which is the escape hatch for pages that have to be generated. The script builds a package that uses all of these and prints the DESCRIPTION that roxygen2 completed and the two Rd files.

# More tags: @include (Collate), @template, @evalRd and @md.
pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "other")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "man-roxygen"))
writeLines(c(
  "Package: other",
  "Title: More Tags",
  "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Description: Shows a few more roxygen2 tags.",
  "License: MIT",
  "Encoding: UTF-8"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))

# A template: a file in man-roxygen/ with roxygen text, used by @template.
writeLines(r"(#' @section Loan period:
#' A loan is overdue after <%= days %> days.
)", file.path(pkg, "man-roxygen", "period.R"))

writeLines(r"(#' Base function
#' @export
base_fn <- function() 1
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "a-base.R"))

writeLines(r"(#' @include a-base.R
NULL

#' Overdue
#'
#' Plain Rd here, markdown is off: \code{x} and \emph{y}.
#' @template period
#' @templateVar days 21
#' @evalRd paste0("\\note{This page lists ", length(letters), " letters.}")
#' @export
overdue <- function() base_fn()

#' Markdown on for one block
#'
#' This has `code`, and *emphasis*.
#' @md
#' @export
md_block <- function() 1
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "b-overdue.R"))

invisible(capture.output(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg), type = "message"))
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")), sep = "\n")
#> Package: other
#> Title: More Tags
#> Version: 0.0.1
#> Description: Shows a few more roxygen2 tags.
#> License: MIT
#> Encoding: UTF-8
#> Config/roxygen2/version: 8.1.1
#> Collate:
#>     'a-base.R'
#>     'b-overdue.R'
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "overdue.Rd")), sep = "\n")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/b-overdue.R
#> \name{overdue}
#> \alias{overdue}
#> \title{Overdue}
#> \usage{
#> overdue()
#> }
#> \description{
#> Plain Rd here, markdown is off: \code{x} and \emph{y}.
#> }
#> \section{Loan period}{
#>
#> A loan is overdue after 21 days.
#> }
#>
#> \note{This page lists 26 letters.}
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "md_block.Rd")), sep = "\n")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/b-overdue.R
#> \name{md_block}
#> \alias{md_block}
#> \title{Markdown on for one block}
#> \usage{
#> md_block()
#> }
#> \description{
#> This has \code{code}, and \emph{emphasis}.
#> }

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Other tags

Collate: was added to DESCRIPTION with the two files in the order the @include tag demanded. The template inserted a section "Loan period" in which <%= days %> was replaced by 21, @evalRd added a \note whose text was computed (26 letters), and the third block shows @md: the whole package has markdown off, so the first function is written in plain Rd (\code{x}, \emph{y}) and the second, with @md, is translated from markdown.

Messages roxygen2 prints

roxygen2 reports mistakes as it documents, and the reports are easy to miss in a long log. The script documents a package with four common ones: a one-line tag that spans two lines, an unknown tag, an S3 method that is not exported, and a @param for an argument that does not exist. It also has a paragraph that begins with a number and a full stop, which markdown reads as a list.

# Messages roxygen2 prints for common mistakes in a throwaway package.
pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "warn")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  "Package: warn",
  "Title: Mistakes",
  "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Description: Shows roxygen2 messages.",
  "License: MIT",
  "Encoding: UTF-8",
  "Config/roxygen2/markdown: TRUE"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))

writeLines(r"(#' Two lines for a one-line tag
#'
#' The edition is on page
#' 1. Clearly not a list, but commonmark makes one.
#' @concept first
#'   second
#' @param y An argument that does not exist
#' @param x Fine.
#' @export
one <- function(x) x

#' A method that is not exported
#'
#' @param x Anything.
#' @param ... Not used.
print.one <- function(x, ...) x

#' Unknown tag
#' @retruns A value.
#' @param x Anything.
two <- function(x) x
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "bad.R"))

msg <- capture.output(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg), type = "message")
sub(pkg, "~/warn", msg, fixed = TRUE)
#>  [1] "First time using roxygen2. Upgrading automatically..."
#>  [2] "ℹ Setting Config/roxygen2/version to \"8.1.1\""
#>  [3] "ℹ Loading warn"
#>  [4] "✖ bad.R:5: @concept must be only 1 line long, not 2."
#>  [5] "ℹ The first line is \"first\""
#>  [6] "✖ bad.R:19: @retruns is not a known tag."
#>  [7] "✖ bad.R:16: S3 method `print.one` needs @export or @exportS3Method tag."
#>  [8] "Writing 'NAMESPACE'"
#>  [9] "Writing 'one.Rd'"
#> [10] "Writing 'print.one.Rd'"
#> [11] "Writing 'two.Rd'"

# The line that began with 1. became a list item, and the @param for the
# argument y that does not exist was written to the page anyway.
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "one.Rd")), sep = "\n")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/bad.R
#> \name{one}
#> \alias{one}
#> \title{Two lines for a one-line tag}
#> \usage{
#> one(x)
#> }
#> \arguments{
#> \item{x}{Fine.}
#>
#> \item{y}{An argument that does not exist}
#> }
#> \description{
#> The edition is on page
#> \enumerate{
#> \item Clearly not a list, but commonmark makes one.
#> }
#> }
#> \concept{first
#>   second}

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: roxygenise

Each message starts with a cross, names the file and the line of the block, and says what is wrong: @concept takes one line (the check is new in roxygen2 8.0.0 and covers the tags listed above), @retruns is not a known tag, and print.one is a method without @export. Two mistakes passed without a message. The line that began with 1. became the item of an \enumerate, because commonmark reads it as a list; the fix is to rephrase the sentence or to escape the full stop. And the @param y for an argument that does not exist was written to the page anyway (\item{y}{An argument that does not exist}); that one is found by R CMD check, in the step shown next.

Checking the documentation

The loop of a package author is edit, devtools::document(), read the warnings, check. devtools::check_man() is the shortcut for the documentation part: it documents the package and runs the Rd checks of R CMD check (tools::checkDocFiles() and friends) without the rest. The script breaks a copy of shelf on purpose in three ways, a new argument without a tag, a tag for an argument that does not exist with a link to a missing topic, and an exported function with no page, and shows what each tool reports.

# The quick loop: document the package and check only its documentation.
# Here on a copy of the package that is broken on purpose, in three ways.
src <- normalizePath(".")
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "copy")
dir.create(tmp)
invisible(file.copy(src, tmp, recursive = TRUE))
pkg <- file.path(tmp, basename(src))

f <- file.path(pkg, "R", "loans.R")
code <- readLines(f)

# 1. A new argument without a @param.
code <- sub("^loans_per_month <- function\\(loans\\) \\{",
            "loans_per_month <- function(loans, by = \"month\") {", code)

# 2. A @param for an argument that does not exist, with a link to a topic that
#    does not exist, in the block of loan_summary().
at <- which(code == "#' @inheritParams overdue_loans")[[1L]]
param <- "#' @param period Not an argument, see [no_such_topic()]."
code <- append(code, param, after = at)
writeLines(code, f)

# document() and the Rd checks of R CMD check in one call.
devtools::check_man(pkg)
#> ℹ Updating shelf documentation
#> ℹ Loading shelf
#> shelf 0.1.0: loan period is 21 days
#> ✖ loans.R:47: @param Could not resolve link to topic "no_such_topic" in the
#>   dependencies or base packages..
#> ℹ If you haven't documented "no_such_topic" yet, or just changed its name, this
#>   is normal. Once "no_such_topic" is documented, this warning goes away.
#> ℹ Make sure that the name of the topic is spelled correctly.
#> ℹ Always list the linked package as a dependency.
#> ℹ Alternatively, you can fully qualify the link with a package name.
#> Writing 'loan_summary.Rd'
#> Writing 'loans_per_month.Rd'
#> ℹ Checking documentation...
#> Missing link(s) in Rd file 'loan_summary.Rd':
#>   ‘no_such_topic’
#>
#> See section 'Cross-references' in the 'Writing R Extensions' manual.
#> Documented arguments not in \usage in Rd file 'loan_summary.Rd':
#>   ‘period’
#>
#> Undocumented arguments in Rd file 'loans_per_month.Rd'
#>   ‘by’
#>

# 3. An exported function with no help page at all.
cat("undocumented_fn <- function() 1\n", file = f, append = TRUE)
cat("export(undocumented_fn)\n", file = file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"),
    append = TRUE)
tools::undoc(dir = pkg)
#> Undocumented code objects:
#>   ‘undocumented_fn’

Source: devtools package documentation: check_man

The output has three parts. The roxygen2 warning is the cross line about the unresolved link, produced while documenting. The Rd checks come after "Checking documentation…​": "Missing link(s)" for the link that cannot be resolved, "Documented arguments not in \usage" for period, which loan_summary() does not have, and "Undocumented arguments" for the new argument by of loans_per_month(). The last call, tools::undoc(), is the check behind "checking for missing documentation entries": it lists the exported objects that have no help page. tools::codoc() compares the usage with the code, and tools::checkDocFiles() the arguments with the \arguments sections. The same broken copy under the real tools, R CMD build and R CMD check, fails three steps; the platform lines at the top of the log are left out and only the documentation steps are shown:

# The same broken copy of the package, checked with R CMD build and R CMD check.
src <- normalizePath(".")
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "copy")
dir.create(tmp)
invisible(file.copy(src, tmp, recursive = TRUE))
pkg <- file.path(tmp, basename(src))

f <- file.path(pkg, "R", "loans.R")
code <- readLines(f)
code <- sub("^loans_per_month <- function\\(loans\\) \\{",
            "loans_per_month <- function(loans, by = \"month\") {", code)
at <- which(code == "#' @inheritParams overdue_loans")[[1L]]
param <- "#' @param period Not an argument, see [no_such_topic()]."
code <- append(code, param, after = at)
code <- c(code, "undocumented_fn <- function() 1")
writeLines(code, f)
invisible(capture.output(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg), type = "message"))
cat("export(undocumented_fn)\n", file = file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"),
    append = TRUE)

# R CMD build and R CMD check run in the directory that holds the package.
r_cmd <- \(...) {
  withr::with_dir(tmp, system2("R", c("CMD", ...),
                               stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE))
}
invisible(r_cmd("build", "--no-build-vignettes", "shelf"))
res <- r_cmd("check", "--no-manual", "--ignore-vignettes", "--no-tests",
             "shelf_0.1.0.tar.gz")

# The platform lines at the top of the log are left out.
first <- grep("checking Rd files", res)
last <- grep("checking Rd contents", res)
res[first:last]
#>  [1] "* checking Rd files ... OK"
#>  [2] "* checking Rd metadata ... OK"
#>  [3] "* checking Rd cross-references ... WARNING"
#>  [4] "Missing link(s) in Rd file 'loan_summary.Rd':"
#>  [5] "  ‘no_such_topic’"
#>  [6] ""
#>  [7] "See section 'Cross-references' in the 'Writing R Extensions' manual."
#>  [8] "* checking for missing documentation entries ... WARNING"
#>  [9] "Undocumented code objects:"
#> [10] "  ‘undocumented_fn’"
#> [11] "All user-level objects in a package should have documentation entries."
#> [12] "See chapter ‘Writing R documentation files’ in the ‘Writing R"
#> [13] "Extensions’ manual."
#> [14] "* checking for code/documentation mismatches ... OK"
#> [15] "* checking Rd \\usage sections ... WARNING"
#> [16] "Documented arguments not in \\usage in Rd file 'loan_summary.Rd':"
#> [17] "  ‘period’"
#> [18] ""
#> [19] "Undocumented arguments in Rd file 'loans_per_month.Rd'"
#> [20] "  ‘by’"
#> [21] ""
#> [22] "Functions with \\usage entries need to have the appropriate \\alias"
#> [23] "entries, and all their arguments documented."
#> [24] "The \\usage entries must correspond to syntactically valid R code."
#> [25] "See chapter ‘Writing R documentation files’ in the ‘Writing R"
#> [26] "Extensions’ manual."
#> [27] "* checking Rd contents ... OK"
grep("^Status", res, value = TRUE)
#> [1] "Status: 3 WARNINGs"

Source: Writing R Extensions: Checking packages

Each of the three mistakes is a WARNING, and the package would be refused on CRAN with any of them. The passing log of the real package, shown at the start of this page, has all of those steps as OK. Do not run these checks by hand each time: devtools::check() does them, and the lintr and testthat pages show the other parts of the loop.

Documenting data, the package and classes

Functions are the easy case. Three other kinds of object need their own habits: data sets, which are not exported and are documented by name; the package itself, which has an overview page; and classes of the four object systems, which are documented through their constructors, generics and methods.

Data sets

A data set is not a function and is not exported: it lives in data/ (the shelf package builds data/books.rda and data/loans.rda from the CSV files in data-raw/ with usethis::use_data()) and it is documented by a block above a string with the name of the data set. The block for books is in R/data.R; the data are made by the script data-raw/books.R, which the package keeps (and leaves out of the tarball through .Rbuildignore) so that the data can be rebuilt. An excerpt of ~/shelf/R/data.R:

#' The shelf catalogue
#'
#' Sixteen books of a small library, as they were typed into the catalogue:
#' titles with stray blanks and inconsistent case, two spellings of one
#' author, genres in several spellings, hyphenated and bare ISBNs (one
#' missing, one with a wrong check digit) and missing years and page counts.
#' [clean_books()] tidies it.
#'
#' @format A data frame with 16 rows and 6 columns:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{title}{Title (character).}
#'   \item{author}{Author (character).}
#'   \item{isbn}{ISBN-13, hyphenated or bare (character).}
#'   \item{year}{Publication year (integer).}
#'   \item{genre}{Genre (character).}
#'   \item{pages}{Number of pages (integer).}
#' }
#' @source Synthetic data generated for this package; the ISBNs have valid
#'   check digits but are not the ISBNs of real books.
#' @family datasets
"books"

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Documenting datasets

The two tags that are specific to data are @format, which describes the structure (for a data frame, one entry per column, as a \describe list that markdown cannot yet write, so this is one of the few places where Rd is written inside a roxygen2 comment), and @source, which says where the data come from. roxygen2 turns the block into the Rd file below. Note that the usage is just books, the name of the object: that is the form for a package with LazyData: true (the shelf DESCRIPTION has it); for a package without lazy data the usage is written data(books), as roxygen2 8.0.0 does. Documenting a data set with its object (x <- 1:10 followed by a block) no longer adds \docType{data}, \keyword{datasets} and a format section since roxygen2 8.0.0; the quoted name is the supported form, and it still writes them.

% Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
% Please edit documentation in R/data.R
\docType{data}
\name{books}
\alias{books}
\title{The shelf catalogue}
\format{
A data frame with 16 rows and 6 columns:
\describe{
\item{title}{Title (character).}
\item{author}{Author (character).}
\item{isbn}{ISBN-13, hyphenated or bare (character).}
\item{year}{Publication year (integer).}
\item{genre}{Genre (character).}
\item{pages}{Number of pages (integer).}
}
}
\source{
Synthetic data generated for this package; the ISBNs have valid
check digits but are not the ISBNs of real books.
}
\usage{
books
}
\description{
Sixteen books of a small library, as they were typed into the catalogue:
titles with stray blanks and inconsistent case, two spellings of one
author, genres in several spellings, hyphenated and bare ISBNs (one
missing, one with a wrong check digit) and missing years and page counts.
\code{\link[=clean_books]{clean_books()}} tidies it.
}
\seealso{
Other datasets:
\code{\link{loans}}
}
\concept{datasets}
\keyword{datasets}

Source: Writing R Extensions: Documenting data sets

The page is what a user sees with ?books. The conversion of the same file to text, with the \describe items that R 4.6.0 renders with a line break after each label:

# How the page of a data set renders in a terminal.
tools::Rd2txt("man/books.Rd", options = list(underline_titles = FALSE))
#> The shelf catalogue
#>
#> Description:
#>
#>      Sixteen books of a small library, as they were typed into the
#>      catalogue: titles with stray blanks and inconsistent case, two
#>      spellings of one author, genres in several spellings, hyphenated
#>      and bare ISBNs (one missing, one with a wrong check digit) and
#>      missing years and page counts. ‘clean_books()’ tidies it.
#>
#> Usage:
#>
#>      books
#>
#> Format:
#>
#>      A data frame with 16 rows and 6 columns:
#>
#>      title
#>           Title (character).
#>
#>      author
#>           Author (character).
#>
#>      isbn
#>           ISBN-13, hyphenated or bare (character).
#>
#>      year
#>           Publication year (integer).
#>
#>      genre
#>           Genre (character).
#>
#>      pages
#>           Number of pages (integer).
#>
#> Source:
#>
#>      Synthetic data generated for this package; the ISBNs have valid
#>      check digits but are not the ISBNs of real books.
#>
#> See Also:
#>
#>      Other datasets: ‘loans’
#>

Source: R documentation: Rd2txt, Rd2HTML, Rd2latex and Rd2ex

The manual’s rules for data pages are two. One data object per Rd file (the usage is books or data(books)), and the keyword datasets. The script that builds the data is a documentation file in a sense too: it is the record of where the data come from, and usethis::use_data_raw() creates it.

# Build the `books` and `loans` datasets from the CSV files in data-raw/.
books <- read.csv("data-raw/books.csv")
loans <- read.csv("data-raw/loans.csv", colClasses = "character")
loans$loan_date <- as.Date(loans$loan_date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
loans$return_date <- as.Date(loans$return_date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
usethis::use_data(books, loans, overwrite = TRUE)

# Internal data: the ISBN-13 check-digit weights used by is_valid_isbn13().
isbn_weights <- rep(c(1L, 3L), length.out = 13L)
usethis::use_data(isbn_weights, internal = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)

Source: usethis package documentation: use_data

Internal data, the isbn_weights vector that is_valid_isbn13() uses, goes to R/sysdata.rda with internal = TRUE and is not documented, since users never see it. R CMD check examines the data: "checking contents of 'data' directory", "checking data for non-ASCII characters", "checking LazyData", "checking data for ASCII and uncompressed saves" and "checking R/sysdata.rda", all OK in the log at the start of this page.

The package itself: "_PACKAGE", README and pkgdown helpers

A package can have an overview page, with the alias pkgname-package, so that ?shelf and package?shelf open it. In roxygen2 the page is written by documenting the string "_PACKAGE": the title, the description and the author section are generated from DESCRIPTION, with the roles of Authors@R, and the block can add a @keywords internal (to keep the page out of the topic index) and the ## usethis namespace: start comments that usethis writes for imports. usethis::use_package_doc() creates the file R/shelf-package.R; usethis::use_readme_rmd() creates a README.Rmd (a README with code that is rendered by devtools::build_readme()), and usethis::use_pkgdown() writes _pkgdown.yml, adds docs to .gitignore and the pkgdown files to .Rbuildignore. The script runs all three on a copy of shelf, in a temporary directory, and then documents the copy.

# The usethis helpers that set up documentation files, run on a copy.
src <- normalizePath(".")
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "uc")
dir.create(tmp)
invisible(file.copy(src, tmp, recursive = TRUE))
pkg <- file.path(tmp, basename(src))

msg <- capture.output(
  usethis::with_project(pkg, {
    usethis::use_pkgdown()
    usethis::use_readme_rmd(open = FALSE)
    usethis::use_package_doc(open = FALSE)
  }),
  type = "message"
)
msg[!grepl("active project", msg)]
#>  [1] "✔ Adding \"^_pkgdown\\\\.yml$\", \"^docs$\", and \"^pkgdown$\" to '.Rbuildignore'."
#>  [2] "✔ Adding \"docs\" to '.gitignore'."
#>  [3] "✔ Writing '_pkgdown.yml'."
#>  [4] "☐ Edit '_pkgdown.yml'."
#>  [5] "✔ Writing 'README.Rmd'."
#>  [6] "✔ Adding \"^README\\\\.Rmd$\" to '.Rbuildignore'."
#>  [7] "☐ Update 'README.Rmd' to include installation instructions."
#>  [8] "☐ Use `devtools::build_readme()` to render 'README.Rmd'."
#>  [9] "✔ Writing 'R/shelf-package.R'."
#> [10] "☐ Run `devtools::document()` to update package-level documentation."

cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "_pkgdown.yml")), sep = "\n")
#> url: ~
#> template:
#>   bootstrap: 5
#>
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "R", "shelf-package.R")), sep = "\n")
#> #' @keywords internal
#> "_PACKAGE"
#>
#> ## usethis namespace: start
#> ## usethis namespace: end
#>
#> ## mockable bindings: start
#> ## mockable bindings: end
#> NULL
head(readLines(file.path(pkg, "README.Rmd")), 4)
#> [1] "---"                     "output: github_document"
#> [3] "---"                     ""

# The package-level page that roxygen2 writes for "_PACKAGE".
invisible(capture.output(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg), type = "message"))
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "shelf-package.Rd")), sep = "\n")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/shelf-package.R
#> \docType{package}
#> \name{shelf-package}
#> \alias{shelf}
#> \alias{shelf-package}
#> \title{shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue}
#> \description{
#> Cleans a small library catalogue and its loans table, validates ISBN-13 strings, and reports overdue loans and overdue rates by genre. Ships the example 'books' and 'loans' datasets used by the documentation.
#> }
#> \author{
#> \strong{Maintainer}: Shelf Maintainers \email{maintainer@example.com} [copyright holder]
#>
#> Authors:
#> \itemize{
#>   \item Shelf Maintainers \email{maintainer@example.com} [copyright holder]
#> }
#>
#> }
#> \keyword{internal}

Source: usethis package documentation: use_package_doc

The generated page shelf-package.Rd has the alias shelf-package and also shelf (roxygen2 adds the alias of the package name unless a function of that name exists), the title and the description of DESCRIPTION, and an author section that lists the maintainer first and then the authors; a person with the roles aut and cre is listed in both parts since roxygen2 8.0.0. Here the only person is the maintainer and the copyright holder. The manual advises that a package overview page be short and that "more extensive documentation is better placed into a package vignette".

S3 classes and methods

An S3 class has no definition to document: the constructor is a function, the generics and methods are functions, and the class is described by the constructor’s page. The roxygen2 article gives the working rules: document a generic like any function and say that it is a generic, document a class by its constructor, and document a method only when it has behaviour of its own, with a link back to the generic; always export S3 methods, because exporting registers them. shelf follows them. The constructor family book(), new_book() and validate_book() is one page (the @rdname book tags put the three blocks into the same file), and the four methods of the class are one more page, book-methods, that has no object of its own: the first block is written above NULL with @name book-methods, and the method blocks are @rdname book-methods and @export. This is an excerpt of ~/shelf/R/book.R:

#' Methods for the `book` class
#'
#' `format()` renders a book as `"<title> (<author>, <year>)"`, `print()`
#' shows that line with a `<book>` marker and `summary()` returns a small
#' `summary.book` object with its own print method.
#'
#' @param x,object A `book` object (for `print.summary.book()`, a
#'   `summary.book` object).
#' @param ... Ignored, present for compatibility with the generics.
#' @returns `format.book()` returns a string; `print.book()` and
#'   `print.summary.book()` return their argument invisibly;
#'   `summary.book()` returns a list of class `summary.book` with the
#'   elements `title`, `has_isbn` and `pages`.
#' @examples
#' b <- book("Salt and Static", "Mara Quill", "978-0-01-400145-3", 2018,
#'           "Mystery", 244)
#' format(b)
#' print(b)
#' s <- summary(b)
#' class(s)
#' s
#' @family book class
#' @name book-methods
NULL

#' @rdname book-methods
#' @export
format.book <- function(x, ...) {
  year <- if (is.na(x$year)) "n.d." else x$year
  sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", x$title, x$author, year)
}

#' @rdname book-methods
#' @export
print.book <- function(x, ...) {

}

}

\code{summary.book()} returns a list of class \code{summary.book} with the

}

\code{format()} renders a book as \code{"<title> (<author>, <year>)"}, \code{print()}
shows that line with a \verb{<book>} marker and \code{summary()} returns a small
\code{summary.book} object with its own print method.
}
\examples{

          "Mystery", 244)
format(b)
print(b)
s <- summary(b)
class(s)
s

Source: Writing R Extensions: Documenting functions, the usage section

The usage is written with \method{format}{book}(x, ...), the macro that says “the S3 method of format for class book”: printed pages show it as format(x, ...), as the manual explains, and the checks compare the full name format.book. The five aliases make help("print.book") and help("summary.book") find the page. The See Also line is the @family book class of both pages. And the description of the methods shows the choice between \code{} and \verb{} again: the markdown code that spells out the format string (a string literal) parses as R and became \code{}, while the marker <book> does not parse and became \verb{}. How S3 methods, generics and dispatch work is in S3 Classes and Generics and in S3 Group Generics and Operator Overloading.

The roxygen2 article adds two more things. For a generic with many methods, the doclisting package (not installed here) generates the list of methods in the page of the generic, either at documentation time with inline R code or at run time with an inline Rd code block, so that the list also shows methods registered by other packages. For a method of a generic defined in another package, @exportS3Method pkg::generic registers the method without importing the generic, as the previous section said.

S4 classes and methods

roxygen2 documents S4 without extra tags for the usual cases. A class is documented above setClass(), with @slot for each slot; a generic is documented above setGeneric() like a function; a method above setMethod() is merged into the generic’s page with @rdname, or, for show, into the class’s page. The generated topics follow the naming rules of Writing R Extensions: Book-class for the class and describe,Book-method for the method, and the NAMESPACE receives exportClasses() and exportMethods() directives. The script documents a small S4 version of the book class in a throwaway package and prints the two Rd files and the NAMESPACE.

# Documenting S4: a class with @slot, a generic and its methods.
pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "s4demo")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  "Package: s4demo",
  "Title: Documenting S4",
  "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Description: Shows how roxygen2 documents S4 classes.",
  "License: MIT",
  "Encoding: UTF-8",
  "Imports: methods",
  "Config/roxygen2/markdown: TRUE"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))

writeLines(r"(#' A book (S4)
#'
#' @slot title Title of the book (a string).
#' @slot author Author (a string).
#' @slot isbn ISBN-13 without hyphens (a string).
#' @slot year Publication year (an integer).
#' @slot genre Genre (a string).
#' @slot pages Number of pages (an integer).
#' @export
setClass("Book", slots = c(
  title = "character", author = "character", isbn = "character",
  year = "integer", genre = "character", pages = "integer"
))

#' Describe an object
#'
#' @param x An object.
#' @returns A string.
#' @export
setGeneric("describe", function(x) standardGeneric("describe"))

#' @rdname describe
#' @export
setMethod("describe", "Book", function(x) x@title)

#' @param object A [Book-class] object.
#' @rdname Book-class
#' @export
setMethod("show", "Book", function(object) {
  cat("<Book>", object@title, "\n")
})
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "book.R"))

invisible(capture.output(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg), type = "message"))
list.files(file.path(pkg, "man"))
#> [1] "Book-class.Rd" "describe.Rd"
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "Book-class.Rd")), sep = "\n")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/book.R

cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "describe.Rd")), sep = "\n")

#> % Please edit documentation in R/book.R
#> \name{describe}

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Documenting S4

The class page has a Slots section built from the @slot tags, an alias Book-class and, because the show method was added to it with @rdname Book-class, an alias show,Book-method and a usage written with \S4method{show}{Book}(object). The generic page has the alias of each method, describe,Book-method, and lists the method’s usage after the generic’s. Writing R Extensions says that every user-visible S4 class and method should have at least an alias in one of the package’s Rd files, and that a package which only adds methods to a generic defined elsewhere documents its methods, not the generic. The S4 classes themselves are the subject of S4 Classes and Methods; the methods package has promptClass() and promptMethods() for the older, manual route.

R6 classes

An R6 class is an environment of methods and fields built by R6::R6Class(), and the documentation of its members is written inside the class definition, above each member, in comments. roxygen2 produces one page for the class with the fields, the active bindings, an index of the methods and a subsection for each method with its usage, arguments and return value, links to the methods of the superclass and an example if there is one. @field documents a field or an active binding, @description and @param a method, and the method blocks may also carry @returns and @examples. The R6 option of roxygen2 is on by default. The script documents a small R6 class and prints the beginning of the generated page (the file has 94 lines).

# Documenting R6: fields and methods are documented inside the class.
pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "r6demo")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  "Package: r6demo",
  "Title: Documenting R6",
  "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Description: Shows how roxygen2 documents R6 classes.",
  "License: MIT",
  "Encoding: UTF-8",
  "Imports: R6",
  "Config/roxygen2/markdown: TRUE"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))

writeLines(r"(#' A shelf of books (R6)
#'
#' Keeps the titles on one shelf.
#' @export
Shelf <- R6::R6Class("Shelf",
  public = list(
    #' @field name Name of the shelf.
    name = NULL,

    #' @description
    #' Create a shelf.
    #' @param name Name of the shelf.
    #' @returns A new `Shelf`.
    initialize = function(name) {
      self$name <- name
    },

    #' @description
    #' Add a title.
    #' @param title Title to add.
    #' @returns The shelf, invisibly, so calls can be chained.
    add = function(title) {
      private$titles <- c(private$titles, title)
      invisible(self)
    }
  ),
  active = list(
    #' @field size Number of titles (read-only).
    size = function() length(private$titles)
  ),
  private = list(titles = character())
)
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "shelf.R"))

invisible(capture.output(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg), type = "message"))
list.files(file.path(pkg, "man"))
#> [1] "Shelf.Rd"
shelf_rd <- readLines(file.path(pkg, "man", "Shelf.Rd"))
length(shelf_rd)
#> [1] 94
cat(head(shelf_rd, 44), sep = "\n")

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Documenting R6

The page is a long Rd file whose structure is out of the ordinary: the fields and active bindings are \describe lists inside HTML-only \if{html}{\out{<div>}} wrappers, the methods are \subsection blocks with an anchor (method-Shelf-initialize) so that the index can link to them, and usage is written as Shelf$new(name) for the constructor and obj$method(args) for the others. The same article lists what roxygen2 8.0.0 added: methods added with $set() can be documented with a block above the $set() call; @R6method Class$method documents methods anywhere; @noRd before a method hides it; classes inherit parameter documentation from the overridden method of their superclass and fields from their superclasses; the initialize() method inherits the documentation of the fields of the same name; and @returns works in method blocks. How R6 classes work is in Reference Classes and R6. roxygen2 documents reference classes (from setRefClass()) with @field too.

S7 classes

S7 is a newer object system; roxygen2 8.0.0 added initial support for it, and S7 0.2.2 is described by its authors as somewhat experimental, so the details below are those of these versions and may change. A class is documented like its constructor function, because new_class() returns one: @param documents the arguments, which are the properties, @returns the object, and @prop the properties that are not constructor arguments, such as a read-only computed property. A generic made with new_generic() is documented like any function. A method registered with method(generic, class) <- fn is detected automatically and documented with a usage line of the form "S7 method for class". The script documents all three in a throwaway package, whose .onLoad() calls S7::methods_register() as an S7 package must, and prints the three generated files.

# Documenting S7 (roxygen2 8.x with S7 0.2.2): class, generic and method.
pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "s7demo")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  "Package: s7demo",
  "Title: Documenting S7",
  "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Description: Shows how roxygen2 documents S7 classes.",
  "License: MIT",
  "Encoding: UTF-8",
  "Depends: R (>= 4.3.0)",
  "Imports: S7",
  "Config/roxygen2/markdown: TRUE"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))

writeLines(r"(#' A book (S7)
#'
#' @param title Title of the book.
#' @param year Publication year.
#' @prop age Age of the book in 2026 (read-only).
#' @returns A `Book` object.
#' @export
Book <- S7::new_class("Book",
  properties = list(
    title = S7::class_character,
    year = S7::class_integer,
    age = S7::new_property(
      S7::class_integer,
      getter = function(self) 2026L - self@year
    )
  )
)

#' Describe an object
#'
#' @param x An object.
#' @param ... Not used.
#' @returns A string.
#' @export
describe <- S7::new_generic("describe", "x")

#' Describe a book
#'
#' The description of a [Book] is its title; see [describe()].
#'
#' @param x A [Book].
#' @param ... Not used.
#' @returns The title.
S7::method(describe, Book) <- function(x, ...) x@title

.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  S7::methods_register()
}
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "book.R"))

invisible(capture.output(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg), type = "message"))
man <- file.path(pkg, "man")
list.files(man)
#> [1] "Book.Rd"                        "describe-s7demo-Book-method.Rd"
#> [3] "describe.Rd"
cat(readLines(file.path(man, "Book.Rd")), sep = "\n")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/book.R
#> \name{Book}
#> \alias{Book}
#> \title{A book (S7)}
#> \usage{
#> Book(title = character(0), year = integer(0))
#> }
#> \arguments{
#> \item{title}{Title of the book.}
#>
#> \item{year}{Publication year.}
#> }
#> \value{
#> A \code{Book} object.
#> }
#> \description{
#> A book (S7)
#> }
#> \section{Additional properties}{
#>
#> \describe{
#> \item{\code{@age}}{Age of the book in 2026 (read-only).}
#> }}
#>
method_rd <- list.files(man, pattern = "method", full.names = TRUE)
cat(readLines(method_rd), sep = "\n")
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in R/book.R
#> \name{describe,s7demo::Book-method}
#> \alias{describe,s7demo::Book-method}
#> \title{Describe a book}
#> \usage{
#> ## S7 method for class <s7demo::Book>
#> \special{describe(x, ...)}
#> }
#> \arguments{
#> \item{x}{A \link{Book}.}
#>
#> \item{...}{Not used.}
#> }
#> \value{
#> The title.
#> }
#> \description{
#> The description of a \link{Book} is its title; see \code{\link[=describe]{describe()}}.
#> }
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE")), sep = "\n")
#> # Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#>
#> export(Book)
#> export(describe)

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Documenting S7

The class page has the constructor’s usage (Book(title = character(0), year = integer(0))), the two arguments and an "Additional properties" section for @age; the generic is a plain function page; and the method got a page of its own, named describe,s7demo::Book-method after the generic and the class, with a usage that roxygen2 8.1.1 wraps in \special{} (which removed a "codoc mismatch" note in R CMD check). The NAMESPACE has the two export() lines and nothing for the method, because the method is registered by methods_register() at load time and needs no @export. roxygen2 recognises the walrus := as an assignment since 8.1.1, so Book := new_class("Book") is documented like Book <- new_class("Book"). The S7 package and its objects are described in The S7 Object System.

Vignettes

A help page documents one function. A vignette documents how the functions work together: a long-form guide, written in a literate format in which prose and R code are mixed, whose code is run when the document is built, so that the output it shows is real and a change that breaks it is noticed. R’s name for the idea (and for the document) is "vignette", and it is part of the package system: sources live in vignettes/, R CMD build turns them into HTML or PDF in inst/doc, the installed package has them in its doc directory, vignette() and browseVignettes() find them, and R CMD check runs their code and checks that the outputs are up to date. Sweave is the engine that ships with R, for LaTeX documents with the extension .Rnw; every other engine is provided by a package, so a package with vignettes in another format says which in DESCRIPTION.

The files and the fields

The shelf vignette is an R Markdown file, vignettes/shelf.Rmd, processed by knitr (1.52) and rmarkdown (2.32), which uses Pandoc for the final conversion to HTML. Three things in DESCRIPTION make that work: Suggests: knitr, rmarkdown (the packages must be available when the package is built and checked, and are not needed to use it), VignetteBuilder: knitr (the name of the package that provides the vignette engine; without the field, R CMD check does not know that the package has non-Sweave vignettes) and, in the file itself, a \VignetteEngine line. The file, as usethis::use_vignette() created it and as the package has it, is the following. The vignette: block in the YAML header carries the three lines that R reads (the %\Vignette... lines are comments for R and are ignored by Pandoc), and output: rmarkdown::html_vignette selects an HTML format with a light style and small output that was designed for package vignettes.

---
title: "Analysing library loans with shelf"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Analysing library loans with shelf}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

The shelf package ships a small, deliberately messy library catalogue and
its loans, and the few functions needed to clean them and answer two
questions: which loans are overdue, and how the overdue rate differs by
genre. This vignette walks through that analysis with a fixed reference
date so that its results do not change from one build to the next.

```{r setup}
library(shelf)
today <- as.Date("2026-06-30")
```

## Cleaning the catalogue

```{r clean}
catalogue <- clean_books(books)
head(catalogue, 4)
table(catalogue$genre)
```

## Overdue loans

```{r overdue}
out <- overdue_loans(loans, today = today)
nrow(out)
head(out[order(-out$days_out), ], 5)
```

## Overdue rate by genre

```{r summary}
loan_summary(loans, catalogue, today = today)
```

## Loans per month

```{r months, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
monthly <- loans_per_month(loans)
barplot(monthly$loans, names.arg = monthly$month, las = 2,
        main = "Loans per month", ylab = "Loans")
```

Source: Writing R Extensions: Writing package vignettes

The metadata lines are \VignetteIndexEntry{title} (the title in the index of vignettes; it need not equal the document title), \VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown} (package and engine), and \VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} (the encoding of the source, required when the file has non-ASCII characters; without a declaration the encoding of the package is assumed). Others that may be seen are \VignetteDepends (packages needed to build the vignette; since R 4.3.0 tools::buildVignettes() has an argument skip that R CMD check uses to skip, and note, vignettes whose dependencies are not available) and \VignetteKeyword. They are read at installation time into the file Meta/vignette.rds, and tools::vignetteInfo() reads them from a source file. The first chunk, include = FALSE, sets collapse = TRUE and comment = "#>" for all chunks, which is why the output of the vignette has the same #> look as the outputs on this page.

usethis::use_vignette() is the helper that writes the template, and makes the changes in DESCRIPTION and .gitignore that go with it. The script creates a second vignette in a copy of the package. It also shows that the helper accepts a .qmd name: in that case it would require the quarto R package, which is not installed here, and writes VignetteBuilder: quarto instead (this is what the source of the function in the image does; the Quarto vignettes below are described and not run).

# usethis::use_vignette() on a copy of the package: a second vignette.
src <- normalizePath(".")
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "vig")
dir.create(tmp)
invisible(file.copy(src, tmp, recursive = TRUE))
pkg <- file.path(tmp, basename(src))

msg <- capture.output(
  usethis::with_project(
    pkg,
    usethis::use_vignette("loans-by-genre", "Overdue loans by genre")
  ),
  type = "message"
)
msg[!grepl("active project", msg)]
#> [1] "✔ Writing 'vignettes/loans-by-genre.Rmd'."
#> [2] "☐ Edit 'vignettes/loans-by-genre.Rmd'."
list.files(file.path(pkg, "vignettes"), all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)
#> [1] ".gitignore"         "loans-by-genre.Rmd" "shelf.Rmd"
cat(readLines(file.path(pkg, "vignettes", "loans-by-genre.Rmd")), sep = "\n")
#> ---
#> title: "Overdue loans by genre"
#> output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
#> vignette: >
#>   %\VignetteIndexEntry{Overdue loans by genre}
#>   %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
#>   %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
#> ---
#>
#> ```{r, include = FALSE}
#> knitr::opts_chunk$set(
#>   collapse = TRUE,
#>   comment = "#>"
#> )
#> ```
#>
#> ```{r setup}
#> library(shelf)
#> ```
# The end of DESCRIPTION, where the helper works.
desc <- readLines(file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))
desc[seq(grep("^Suggests", desc), length(desc))]
#>  [1] "Suggests: "                 "    knitr,"
#>  [3] "    rmarkdown,"             "    testthat (>= 3.0.0),"
#>  [5] "    withr"                  "Config/testthat/edition: 3"
#>  [7] "Depends: "                  "    R (>= 4.1.0)"
#>  [9] "VignetteBuilder: knitr"     "LazyData: true"

Source: usethis package documentation: use_vignette

The helper wrote vignettes/loans-by-genre.Rmd with the header and the setup chunk of the first vignette, and made sure that knitr and rmarkdown are in Suggests and that VignetteBuilder is knitr: here they already were, so the end of DESCRIPTION did not change. For a package that did not have them, the helper adds the entries, and it adds inst/doc to .gitignore, so that the built vignettes stay out of the repository. vignettes/.gitignore is a second line of defence:

*.html
*.R

Source: usethis package documentation: use_vignette

The two patterns keep the .html and .R files, which are what building the vignette in place leaves in vignettes/, out of version control. They are build products: the tarball gets them in inst/doc.

Building: R CMD build and the tarball

R CMD build is where the vignettes are rendered. It installs the package into a temporary library (the vignette calls library(shelf)), runs the engine on every file in vignettes/, and copies the sources and the outputs into inst/doc of the tarball, which is also what lets an author use private packages, screenshots and anything else that only exists on one machine. R keeps the outputs in the tarball so that they need not be rebuilt at installation, and R CMD check verifies that the outputs are not older than the sources. The script builds a copy of shelf with R CMD build and lists the files of the tarball that matter, and then builds it again with --no-build-vignettes:

# R CMD build renders the vignette into inst/doc of the tarball.
src <- normalizePath(".")
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "build")
dir.create(tmp)
invisible(file.copy(src, tmp, recursive = TRUE))
r_cmd <- \(...) {
  withr::with_dir(tmp, system2("R", c("CMD", ...),
                               stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE))
}
tarball <- file.path(tmp, "shelf_0.1.0.tar.gz")
in_tarball <- \(pattern) {
  grep(pattern, utils::untar(tarball, list = TRUE), value = TRUE)
}

r_cmd("build", "shelf")
#> [1] "* checking for file ‘shelf/DESCRIPTION’ ... OK"
#> [2] "* preparing ‘shelf’:"
#> [3] "* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... OK"
#> [4] "* installing the package (it is needed to build vignettes)"
#> [5] "* creating vignettes ... OK"
#> [6] "* checking for LF line-endings in source and make files and shell scripts"
#> [7] "* checking for empty or unneeded directories"
#> [8] "* building ‘shelf_0.1.0.tar.gz’"
#> [9] ""
in_tarball("vignettes|inst/doc|build/")
#> [1] "shelf/build/"              "shelf/build/vignette.rds"
#> [3] "shelf/inst/doc/"           "shelf/inst/doc/shelf.R"
#> [5] "shelf/inst/doc/shelf.Rmd"  "shelf/inst/doc/shelf.html"
#> [7] "shelf/vignettes/"          "shelf/vignettes/shelf.Rmd"

# The same build without the vignettes (as --no-build-vignettes asks).
unlink(tarball)
r_cmd("build", "--no-build-vignettes", "shelf")
#> [1] "* checking for file ‘shelf/DESCRIPTION’ ... OK"
#> [2] "* preparing ‘shelf’:"
#> [3] "* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... OK"
#> [4] "* checking for LF line-endings in source and make files and shell scripts"
#> [5] "* checking for empty or unneeded directories"
#> [6] "* building ‘shelf_0.1.0.tar.gz’"
#> [7] ""
in_tarball("vignettes|inst/doc|build/")
#> [1] "shelf/vignettes/"          "shelf/vignettes/shelf.Rmd"

# R CMD check notices that the sources have no outputs next to them.
res <- r_cmd("check", "--no-manual", "--no-tests", "--no-examples",
             "shelf_0.1.0.tar.gz")
step <- \(title) {
  i <- grep(title, res, fixed = TRUE)
  res[i:(i + 3L)]
}
step("checking files in ‘vignettes’")
#> [1] "* checking files in ‘vignettes’ ... WARNING"
#> [2] "Files in the 'vignettes' directory but no files in 'inst/doc':"
#> [3] "  ‘shelf.Rmd’"
#> [4] "* checking examples ... SKIPPED"
step("checking package vignettes")
#> [1] "* checking package vignettes ... WARNING"
#> [2] "Directory 'inst/doc' does not exist."
#> [3] "Package vignette without corresponding single PDF/HTML:"
#> [4] "  ‘shelf.Rmd’"
grep("^Status", res, value = TRUE)
#> [1] "Status: 2 WARNINGs"

Source: Writing R Extensions: Building package tarballs

The log of the first build has the step "installing the package (it is needed to build vignettes)" and "creating vignettes …​ OK". The tarball then holds vignettes/shelf.Rmd (the source), inst/doc/shelf.html (the output), inst/doc/shelf.R (the code of the vignette extracted by "tangling"; it is the file that the field R of the object returned by vignette() names) and inst/doc/shelf.Rmd (the source again, so that vignette("shelf") can offer it), and build/vignette.rds, the index that the installation uses. The second build skips the whole step and the tarball only has vignettes/shelf.Rmd. The check of that tarball, at the end of the script, shows why it is not what you want to ship: the source has no output next to it, and two steps give a WARNING ("Files in the 'vignettes' directory but no files in 'inst/doc'" and "Package vignette without corresponding single PDF/HTML"). The option --ignore-vignettes of R CMD check is the escape for a check of such a tarball, as in the earlier script.

The functions behind the commands are in the tools package. tools::buildVignettes() is what R CMD build calls, and the script calls it directly on a copy of the package, after trying the function of devtools that exists for the same purpose, which is deprecated.

# Rendering the vignettes of a source tree without building the tarball.
src <- normalizePath(".")
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "dev")
dir.create(tmp)
invisible(file.copy(src, tmp, recursive = TRUE))
pkg <- file.path(tmp, basename(src))

# devtools::build_vignettes() is deprecated since devtools 2.5.0; in this
# image it also stops, because the package remotes is not installed.
res <- withCallingHandlers(
  tryCatch(devtools::build_vignettes(pkg), error = \(e) conditionMessage(e)),
  warning = \(w) {
    cat("warning:", conditionMessage(w), "\n")
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
#> warning: `build_vignettes()` was deprecated in devtools 2.5.0.
res
#> [1] "The package \"remotes\" is required."

# tools::buildVignettes() is the function under R CMD build.
out <- tools::buildVignettes(dir = pkg, tangle = TRUE)
#> --- re-building ‘shelf.Rmd’ using rmarkdown
#> --- finished re-building ‘shelf.Rmd’
#>
names(out)
#>  [1] "docs"      "names"     "engines"   "patterns"  "encodings" "dir"
#>  [7] "pkgdir"    "msg"       "outputs"   "sources"
basename(out$outputs)
#> [1] "shelf.html"
list.files(file.path(pkg, "vignettes"))
#> [1] "shelf.html" "shelf.R"    "shelf.Rmd"

Source: R documentation: buildVignettes

devtools::build_vignettes() was deprecated in devtools 2.5.0, and in this image it stops with "The package "remotes" is required", because the package remotes is not installed; use devtools::build() (which builds the tarball like R CMD build) or call tools::buildVignettes(). The call returned a list with the vignettes' sources and outputs; shelf.html and shelf.R appeared next to shelf.Rmd in vignettes/, which is why the two files are in vignettes/.gitignore.

Reading the installed vignette

The installed package has the guide and the index that points to it. The script uses vignette(), browseVignettes(), tools::vignetteInfo() and tools::vignetteEngine(); the last shows the engines that knitr registers when it is loaded, which are the values that can follow \VignetteEngine.

# Finding the installed vignette of the package.
v <- vignette(package = "shelf")
class(v)
#> [1] "packageIQR"
data.frame(v$results[, c("Item", "Title"), drop = FALSE], row.names = NULL)
#>    Item                                             Title
#> 1 shelf Analysing library loans with shelf (source, html)

vig <- vignette("shelf", package = "shelf")
class(vig)
#> [1] "vignette"
names(vig)
#> [1] "Package" "Dir"     "Topic"   "File"    "Title"   "R"       "PDF"
basename(vig$File)
#> [1] "shelf.Rmd"
basename(vig$R)
#> [1] "shelf.R"

# The files in the installed doc directory; index.html is made at install time.
list.files(system.file("doc", package = "shelf"))
#> [1] "index.html" "shelf.html" "shelf.R"    "shelf.Rmd"

# browseVignettes() returns the same information (printing it opens a browser).
bv <- browseVignettes("shelf")
class(bv)
#> [1] "browseVignettes"
colnames(bv$shelf)
#> [1] "Package" "Dir"     "Topic"   "File"    "Title"   "R"       "PDF"
unname(bv$shelf[, "Title"])
#> [1] "Analysing library loans with shelf"

# The metadata lines of the source file, as R reads them.
info <- tools::vignetteInfo(system.file("doc", "shelf.Rmd", package = "shelf"))
info$title
#> [1] "Analysing library loans with shelf"
info$engine
#> [1] "knitr::rmarkdown"

# knitr registers its engines when it is loaded.
invisible(loadNamespace("knitr"))
sort(names(tools::vignetteEngine(package = "knitr")))
#>  [1] "knitr::docco_classic"          "knitr::docco_classic_notangle"
#>  [3] "knitr::docco_linear"           "knitr::docco_linear_notangle"
#>  [5] "knitr::knitr"                  "knitr::knitr_notangle"
#>  [7] "knitr::rmarkdown"              "knitr::rmarkdown_notangle"
#>  [9] "knitr::rtyp"                   "knitr::rtyp_notangle"

Source: R documentation: vignette

vignette(package = "shelf") lists the vignettes of the package with the title from \VignetteIndexEntry and the formats available (source, html), vignette("shelf", package = "shelf") returns an object of class vignette that opens in a browser when printed, and browseVignettes() returns the table that the HTML index is built from. The doc directory also has index.html, written at installation from the index entries unless the package supplies its own. For a script that wants the code of the vignette, vignette()$R is the path of shelf.R, which is inst/doc/shelf.R of the tarball. R CMD check examines the same files: "checking installed files from 'inst/doc'", "checking files in 'vignettes'", "checking package vignettes", "checking for unstated dependencies in vignettes" and "checking re-building of vignette outputs" are the steps in the log at the top of the page, and the last one is the one that rebuilds each vignette and fails when a chunk gives an error.

knitr and R Markdown in a vignette

A knitr-based vignette is an ordinary R Markdown document with the header lines above; the knitr site and the rmarkdown site document the chunk options and the output formats. The R chunks are evaluated in order, each chunk’s results and figures are inserted, and the chunk options (collapse, comment, fig.width, eval, echo, include) are knitr’s; a chunk with eval = FALSE is shown and not run, which is how a vignette shows code that needs a service or a long computation. All the chunks run when the package is checked, so a vignette is a test too. Of the engines that knitr registers, listed by the script above, knitr::rmarkdown (R Markdown to HTML or PDF) is the one used here, knitr::knitr processes Sweave-like .Rnw files with knitr, and the names that end in _notangle are the same engines without the extraction of the code. A vignette in HTML needs Pandoc, and one in PDF needs LaTeX.

Four rules keep a vignette from causing trouble on CRAN. Make it deterministic, as the shelf vignette does by fixing the reference date (today <- as.Date("2026-06-30")) instead of asking the system for the current date. Keep it fast, since the CRAN Repository Policy asks for the checks to take as little CPU time as possible (see Publishing to CRAN). Keep files small: PDF or HTML output that is too large is a known problem (the manual mentions a PDF of 72 MB), and the CRAN policy sets a 5 MB guideline for documentation. And use only packages that are declared, because the check "unstated dependencies in vignettes" fails on a package that is used but not listed in Suggests or Imports.

If a document should be on the website of the package but not in the tarball (because it is large, or needs a service), usethis::use_article() creates an "article" that only pkgdown builds, in the next section.

Quarto vignettes

Quarto, the multi-language successor of R Markdown from Posit, can render the same kind of document, and R packages can use it for vignettes. Quarto executes R cells with knitr, so most R Markdown documents render without change. The command-line program is separate from R (version 1.10.19 is installed in the image), and what connects it to the package system is the quarto R package, which registers the vignette engines quarto::html and a PDF one. The setup, as the package’s own article describes it, is VignetteBuilder: quarto in DESCRIPTION, quarto in Suggests, and the header of the .qmd file:

---
title: "Analysing library loans with shelf"
format: html
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Analysing library loans with shelf}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Source: quarto package documentation: Quarto HTML Vignettes

This is a fragment, not run: the quarto R package is not installed in the image, so R CMD build of such a package cannot run here. The Quarto program can render the file by itself, though. The shell script below makes a throwaway directory, writes a .qmd file with that header and one R chunk that loads the installed shelf and counts the overdue loans, and renders it with the program. The plain quarto render ignores the vignette: metadata and uses the default HTML format of Quarto:

export NO_COLOR=1
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
cat > shelf.qmd <<'QMD'
---
title: "Analysing library loans with shelf"
format: html
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Analysing library loans with shelf}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r}
library(shelf)
nrow(overdue_loans(loans, today = as.Date("2026-06-30")))
```
QMD
quarto render shelf.qmd
ls

Source: Quarto: Using R

processing file: shelf.qmd
1/3
2/3 [unnamed-chunk-1]
3/3
output file: shelf.knit.md

pandoc
  to: html
  output-file: shelf.html
  standalone: true
  section-divs: true
  html-math-method: mathjax
  wrap: none
  default-image-extension: png

metadata
  document-css: false
  link-citations: true
  date-format: long
  lang: en
  title: Analysing library loans with shelf
  vignette: |
    %\VignetteIndexEntry{Analysing library loans with shelf} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}

Output created: shelf.html

shelf_files
shelf.html
shelf.qmd

Source: Quarto: Using R

The output shows what a Quarto render looks like: the chunk was executed (1/3, 2/3 [unnamed-chunk-1], 3/3) by knitr, Pandoc was called with the HTML options, and the result is shelf.html and a shelf_files directory. The vignette block is in the listed metadata as plain text, which is how Quarto passes it through; only the quarto R package turns it into an engine. The package’s article states two limits: the HTML vignette engine produces a deliberately minimal format (a standalone file, Bootstrap off, a small stylesheet of its own, and settings that cannot be overridden from the header, although new ones such as toc: true can be added), and an interactive quarto render uses the default HTML format of Quarto and not the vignette one, so only building the package shows the real result. The intermediate files of an authoring workflow (vignettes/*_files) belong in .Rbuildignore and .gitignore. For PDF there is a separate engine; and usethis::use_vignette("name.qmd") sets a package up for Quarto if the quarto R package and pkgdown 2.1.0 or later are installed.

The choice between the two is practical. R Markdown with knitr is the default of the package tooling, has no dependency outside R and Pandoc, and works everywhere R CMD check does. Quarto vignettes need the Quarto program on the machine that builds the package, and give access to Quarto’s features; for a package whose vignettes are an ordinary guide, R Markdown is the shorter road, and the Quarto road is the one for a package that already uses Quarto for its other documents. Reports with Quarto and R Markdown is the page about the formats themselves.

Sweave and other vignette formats

Sweave (.Rnw files, LaTeX with R chunks, run by utils::Sweave() and extracted by Stangle()) is the engine that needs no VignetteBuilder, and the manual’s section on vignettes is written in terms of it; R CMD Sweave and R CMD Stangle are the command-line forms. Documents in inst/doc can be in any format; the manual recommends HTML or PDF, so that users on almost all platforms can read them. New code uses R Markdown or Quarto.

pkgdown websites

pkgdown builds a static website from a package: a home page from README.md (or index.md), a function reference with a page for every Rd topic, the vignettes as "articles", the news from NEWS.md and the authors. Each Rd topic is converted to an HTML page with its links resolved across the site, the examples are run and their output is inserted, and the vignettes are rendered again with the pkgdown layout. The script builds the site of a copy of shelf completely offline: nothing is deployed, and the temporary directories are removed from the log, which is long. It starts with the report of pkgdown_sitrep() on a package with no configuration, adds the smallest _pkgdown.yml and shows what check_pkgdown() reports, completes it, and builds.

# Build the pkgdown site of a copy of the package (offline, nothing deployed).
src <- normalizePath(".")
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "site")
dir.create(tmp)
invisible(file.copy(src, tmp, recursive = TRUE))
pkg <- file.path(tmp, basename(src))
show_error <- \(expr) {
  tryCatch(expr, error = \(e) cat(conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
}

# With no configuration file, pkgdown reports what it would have to guess.
pkgdown::pkgdown_sitrep(pkg)
#> ── Sitrep ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✖ Bootstrap 3 is deprecated; please switch to Bootstrap 5.
#> ℹ Learn more at
#>   <https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2021/12/pkgdown-2-0-0/#bootstrap-5>.
#> ✖ URLs not ok.
#>   No '_pkgdown.yml' found.
#>   See details in `vignette(pkgdown::metadata)`.
#> ✔ Favicons ok.
#> ✔ Open graph metadata ok.
#> ✔ Articles metadata ok.
#> ✔ Reference metadata ok.

# A first _pkgdown.yml: the site URL and a reference index with one group.
writeLines(c(
  "url: https://example.github.io/shelf/",
  "template:",
  "  bootstrap: 5",
  "reference:",
  "  - title: The book class",
  "    contents:",
  "      - book"
), file.path(pkg, "_pkgdown.yml"))

# pkgdown wants the site URL in the URL field of DESCRIPTION, too.
show_error(pkgdown::check_pkgdown(pkg))
#> In DESCRIPTION, URL is missing package url
#> (https://example.github.io/shelf).
#> ℹ See details in `vignette(pkgdown::metadata)`.
cat("URL: https://example.github.io/shelf/\n",
    file = file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"), append = TRUE)

# Every topic that is not internal must be in the reference index.
show_error(pkgdown::check_pkgdown(pkg))
#> In _pkgdown.yml, 8 topics missing from index: "book-methods", "books",
#> "clean_books", "loan_summary", "loans", "loans_per_month", "normalise_isbn",
#> and "overdue_loans".
#> ℹ Either add to the reference index, or use `@keywords internal` to drop from
#>   the index.

# The complete configuration.
writeLines(c(
  "url: https://example.github.io/shelf/",
  "template:",
  "  bootstrap: 5",
  "reference:",
  "  - title: The book class",
  "    desc: Constructor, validator and methods.",
  "    contents:",
  "      - book",
  "      - book-methods",
  "  - title: Cleaning",
  "    contents:",
  "      - clean_books",
  "      - normalise_isbn",
  "  - title: Loans",
  "    contents:",
  "      - overdue_loans",
  "      - loan_summary",
  "      - loans_per_month",
  "  - title: Data",
  "    contents:",
  "      - books",
  "      - loans",
  "articles:",
  "  - title: Analysis",
  "    contents:",
  "      - shelf"
), file.path(pkg, "_pkgdown.yml"))
pkgdown::check_pkgdown(pkg)
#> ✔ No problems found.

log <- capture.output(
  pkgdown::build_site(pkg, preview = FALSE, new_process = FALSE),
  type = "message"
)
# The section headings and the checks of the log; the per-file lines and the
# paths of the temporary directory are left out.
log[grepl("^(──|✔|✖)", log)]
#>  [1] "── Installing package shelf into temporary library ─────────────────────────────"
#>  [2] "── Initialising site ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
#>  [3] "── Building pkgdown site for package shelf ─────────────────────────────────────"
#>  [4] "── Sitrep ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
#>  [5] "✔ URLs ok."

#> [13] "── Building articles ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"

sum(grepl("^Adding redirect", log))

#> [17] "loans_per_month.md"      "loans.html"
