Source: pkgdown package documentation: build_site

Read it in order. With no _pkgdown.yml, pkgdown_sitrep() reports that the URLs are not set ("No '_pkgdown.yml' found") and that Bootstrap 3 is deprecated, so template: bootstrap: 5 is the first line to write. The url is the second: it must be the address where the site will live, and pkgdown wants it also in the URL field of DESCRIPTION, which it reported. The first check_pkgdown() after that complained that eight topics were missing from the reference index: once a reference: field exists, every topic has to appear in it (or be marked @keywords internal), because an index that omits a topic is a broken index. The complete configuration has four groups of reference topics (the class, cleaning, loans and the data) and one group of articles; check_pkgdown() found no problems, and build_site() ran its steps, from installing the package into a temporary library to the search index. The result is a docs directory. Its reference directory has an HTML page for each of the nine topics, an index, and eight further small pages, one for each alias that has no page of its own (the "Adding redirect" messages count them), and articles has shelf.html, the vignette, and an index.

The _pkgdown.yml of this script is a good minimum. Its fields are url, template (the Bootstrap version and the theme), reference (a list of groups, each with a title, an optional desc and a contents list of topic names or selectors such as starts_with("loan")), and articles. The documentation lists more: the navigation bar, the home page sidebar, news, authors, a deploy field, and the headings of the site. Sites are written to docs/ by default; publishing is a step of its own. pkgdown’s recommended path for a GitHub repository is usethis::use_pkgdown_github_pages(), which sets up a GitHub Actions workflow built on the r-lib/actions repository that builds the site on every push and publishes it to GitHub Pages; for another host, pkgdown::build_site() and a copy of docs/ are enough. Both are fragments, not run (they need a remote repository and a token):

usethis::use_pkgdown_github_pages()
pkgdown::build_site()

Source: pkgdown package documentation: Introduction to pkgdown

pkgdown does not create documentation; it publishes what the package has. A site is therefore only as good as the Rd files, the vignettes, the README and the NEWS.md, and the usual problem is the reference index. One more point is worth knowing: pkgdown runs every example, so an example that needs a service must be guarded as for CRAN.

inst/CITATION: how to cite the package

citation() with no argument gives the citation of R, and citation("pkg") the citation of a package. The text comes from the file inst/CITATION if the package has one, and otherwise is built from DESCRIPTION. The file is R code, in the encoding of the package, with one or more calls of bibentry(); it must produce no output when sourced and, because CRAN requires it, it must not call functions such as packageDescription() that assume the package is installed in a library on the search path. The object meta, a parsed version of DESCRIPTION, is available inside the file, so that a title and a version need not be repeated and get out of date. The shelf file is the smallest that works:

bibentry(
  bibtype = "Manual",
  title = "shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue",
  author = person("Shelf", "Maintainers"),
  year = "2026",
  note = "R package version 0.1.0"
)

Source: Writing R Extensions: CITATION files

The script prints the citation of R itself (a good example of the output), the citation of shelf, reads the installed file by hand with readCitationFile(), formats it in text style, and prints what R would have generated if the file did not exist, in the form of the bibentry() call.

# citation(): R itself, the shelf package, and the same data read by hand.
citation()
#> To cite R in publications use:
#>
#>   R Core Team (2026). _R: A Language and Environment for Statistical
#>   Computing_. R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria.
#>   doi:10.32614/R.manuals <https://doi.org/10.32614/R.manuals>.
#>   <https://www.R-project.org/>.
#>
#> A BibTeX entry for LaTeX users is
#>
#>   @Manual{,
#>     title = {R: A Language and Environment for Statistical Computing},
#>     author = {{R Core Team}},
#>     organization = {R Foundation for Statistical Computing},
#>     address = {Vienna, Austria},
#>     year = {2026},
#>     doi = {10.32614/R.manuals},
#>     url = {https://www.R-project.org/},
#>   }
#>
#> We have invested a lot of time and effort in creating R, please cite it
#> when using it for data analysis. See also ‘citation("pkgname")’ for
#> citing R packages.

citation("shelf")
#> To cite package ‘shelf’ in publications use:
#>
#>   Maintainers S (2026). _shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue_. R
#>   package version 0.1.0.
#>
#> A BibTeX entry for LaTeX users is
#>
#>   @Manual{,
#>     title = {shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue},
#>     author = {Shelf Maintainers},
#>     year = {2026},
#>     note = {R package version 0.1.0},
#>   }

# The file the package ships: inst/CITATION is installed as CITATION.
cit <- readCitationFile(system.file("CITATION", package = "shelf"))
class(cit)
#> [1] "citation" "bibentry"
format(cit, style = "text")
#> [1] "Maintainers S (2026). _shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue_. R\npackage version 0.1.0."
cit$title
#> [1] "shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue"

# What would be generated without a CITATION file, as bibentry() code.
print(citation("shelf", auto = TRUE), style = "R")
#> bibentry(bibtype = "Manual",
#>          header = "To cite package ‘shelf’ in publications use:",
#>          title = "shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue",
#>          author = person(given = "Shelf",
#>                          family = "Maintainers",
#>                          role = c("aut", "cre", "cph"),
#>                          email = "maintainer@example.com"),
#>          year = "2026",
#>          note = "R package version 0.1.0")

Source: R documentation: citation

The names are shown as "Maintainers S" because the author is person("Shelf", "Maintainers"), given name Shelf and family name Maintainers. The citation has no url: the CITATION file of shelf had one at first, but R CMD check --as-cran checks URLs and answered that it was a 404, so it was removed, the same trap described in Publishing to CRAN. The auto-generated version (the last call) is the one that R shows when no file exists, and Writing R Extensions suggests starting from it: print(citation("pkg", auto = TRUE), style = "R") prints the code. In R 4.5.0 the auto-generated entries began to include the DOIs that CRAN and Bioconductor assign to their packages. A package with a paper to cite, or one that should be cited in a particular way, adds entries. The second script writes a fuller file in a temporary directory, with two entries, a header on each, and the title and note built from meta, then reads it with readCitationFile() and the description of the installed package as meta:

# A fuller CITATION: the package itself, built from DESCRIPTION, plus a paper.
file <- file.path(tempdir(), "CITATION")
writeLines(r"(
bibentry(
  bibtype = "Manual",
  title = paste0(meta$Package, ": ", meta$Title),
  author = person("Shelf", "Maintainers"),
  year = format(as.Date("2026-06-30"), "%Y"),
  note = paste("R package version", meta$Version),
  header = "To cite the shelf package:"
)

bibentry(
  bibtype = "Article",
  title = "Cleaning a Small Library Catalogue",
  author = c(person("Mara", "Quill"), person("Tomas", "Arden")),
  journal = "Journal of Imaginary Libraries",
  year = "2025",
  volume = "3",
  number = "1",
  pages = "10--20",
  header = "And the method behind it:"
)
)", file)
cit <- readCitationFile(file, meta = packageDescription("shelf"))
length(cit)
#> [1] 2
print(cit)
#> To cite the shelf package:
#>
#>   Maintainers S (2026). _shelf: Tools for a Small Library Catalogue_. R
#>   package version 0.1.0.
#>
#> And the method behind it:
#>
#>   Quill M, Arden T (2025). “Cleaning a Small Library Catalogue.”
#>   _Journal of Imaginary Libraries_, *3*(1), 10-20.
#>
#> To see these entries in BibTeX format, use 'print(<citation>,
#> bibtex=TRUE)', 'toBibtex(.)', or set
#> 'options(citation.bibtex.max=999)'.

Source: R documentation: bibentry

The first entry is computed from meta (paste0(meta$Package, ": ", meta$Title) gave the title shown), and the second is a journal article that does not exist (the journal is imaginary, as the authors are). The header argument of each entry becomes the line above it. citation() prints the text form of every entry and a note about BibTeX; print(cit, bibtex = TRUE) or toBibtex() gives the BibTeX entries. If a bibentry contains LaTeX markup in names or titles, the argument textVersion supplies the plain text to print.

NEWS.md: what changed

A NEWS file is the changelog that news() reads and that users, CRAN and pkgdown show. R looks for it, in order, in inst/NEWS.Rd, NEWS.md (since R 3.6.0, and it needs the commonmark and xml2 packages), NEWS and inst/NEWS. For NEWS.md the format is Markdown: a first-level heading gives the package name and the version (and optionally a date in parentheses), a second-level heading gives a category, and the bullets are the entries. usethis::use_news_md() writes a first file. The shelf file has a heading for version 0.1.0 and one bullet:

# shelf 0.1.0

* Initial version: the `book` class, `clean_books()`, `clean_loans()`,
  `overdue_loans()`, `loan_summary()` and `loans_per_month()`, with the
  `books` and `loans` datasets.

Source: R documentation: news

The script reads the installed file back with news(): the result is a data frame with the version, date, category, text (and an HTML rendering), print() formats it, and news(Version >= "0.1.0", package = "shelf") selects by an expression over the columns.

# news(): the NEWS.md of the installed package, as a data frame.
n <- news(package = "shelf")
class(n)
#> [1] "news_db_from_md" "news_db"         "data.frame"
names(n)
#> [1] "Version"  "Date"     "Category" "Text"     "HTML"
n$Version
#> [1] "0.1.0"
cat(n$Text, sep = "\n")
#>   - Initial version: the book class, clean_books(), clean_loans(),
#>     overdue_loans(), loan_summary() and loans_per_month(), with the
#>     books and loans datasets.

# print() formats the entries; doBrowse = FALSE keeps the text in the console.
print(n, doBrowse = FALSE)
#>                         Changes in version 0.1.0
#>
#>   - Initial version: the book class, clean_books(), clean_loans(),
#>     overdue_loans(), loan_summary() and loans_per_month(), with the
#>     books and loans datasets.

# A query over the entries.
news(Version >= "0.1.0", package = "shelf")$Version
#> [1] "0.1.0"

Source: R documentation: news

The print method shows "Changes in version 0.1.0" and the bullet with the code formatting removed. A good NEWS.md is written for the users, not for the commit log: it says what changed in a way that affects a user, puts the newest version at the top, mentions each deprecated function with its replacement, and names the person or issue only if that helps. R 4.3.0 made R CMD check report problems it meets when reading NEWS.md, so a malformed file is found by the check. pkgdown publishes the file on the "News" page of the site.

README and the other files

A README.md is not part of R’s documentation system but is where people arrive: GitHub shows it, CRAN shows it on the package’s page, and pkgdown uses it as the home page. It should say what the package is for, how to install it and one short example. When the example should run, README.Rmd is rendered to README.md with devtools::build_readme(), as usethis::use_readme_rmd() sets up (the script of the package-page section created one). usethis adds README.Rmd to .Rbuildignore when it creates it, as the output of that script shows. CONTRIBUTING.md and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md are other files of the same kind, and shelf also has a cran-comments.md, the notes that the author sends to CRAN with a submission, which is explained in Publishing to CRAN.

Pitfalls

  • Editing a generated file. A file that starts with "Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand" is overwritten by the next devtools::document(); edit the comment in the R file. The reverse also holds: roxygen2 leaves a hand-written Rd file alone (it says so, as shown above), so a package can mix the two, and a file that was once generated and is now edited by hand must lose its header.

  • Forgetting to document after a change. R CMD build does not run roxygen2: it packages man/ and NAMESPACE as they are. Commit both, run devtools::document() before every commit that touches a tag, and let devtools::check() catch the rest. devtools::load_all() does not regenerate documentation either, and it exposes every function, which hides an S3 method that lacks @export.

  • The percent sign and the braces in Rd. In hand-written Rd, % starts a comment and eats the closing brace, and unbalanced braces are an error: \% and balanced braces. roxygen2 with markdown escapes the percent signs for you; roxygen2 without markdown does not.

  • Examples that cannot run on a check farm. Examples may not need a network, a key, a display or write access outside a temporary directory. \dontrun{} hides code from every check, which reviewers dislike for code that could run; \donttest{} is run by --as-cran since R 4.0.0; @examplesIf runs the example only when its condition holds. Examples are also run by pkgdown and by example().

  • Arguments that do not match. The usage is taken from the code, so a renamed argument shows in the usage at once, but the @param for the old name stays and is reported ("Documented arguments not in \usage"), and the new one is "Undocumented". Run devtools::check_man() after every change of a signature.

  • A description that repeats the title. A block with a title and nothing else gives a page whose description is the title, as the generated page for overdue_rate() above shows. R CMD check accepts it; readers and CRAN reviewers do not.

  • Markdown surprises. A sentence in a comment that starts with 1. becomes a list. [word] becomes a link. A heading level 1 makes a new section. Inline code that does not parse as R becomes \verb{}, not \code{}. Block quotes, inline HTML and horizontal rules are not supported.

  • The warnings of the first run. The first document() of a new package warns about links to topics that are written in the same run, and the second run is clean. If a warning is still there on the second run, the link is wrong, or the linked package is not in DESCRIPTION.

  • The index of a pkgdown site. Once _pkgdown.yml has a reference field, every topic has to be listed in it or be internal. pkgdown::check_pkgdown() finds the missing ones, before a build fails.

  • Non-deterministic vignettes. A vignette that prints the current date, uses a random number without a seed, or reads the current state of a service changes at every build, and a changed output with no changed source confuses reviewers. The shelf vignette fixes the date.

  • Built vignettes in the repository. inst/doc and the files in vignettes/ that the build leaves (*.html, *.R) are products. usethis::use_vignette() ignores them with .gitignore; the tarball gets them from R CMD build.

  • A CITATION file that depends on installation. The file is run when the package is not installed; calling packageDescription() or utils::packageVersion() in it works on the author’s machine and fails on CRAN. Use meta.

  • A PDF manual needs TeX. Without pdflatex, R CMD Rd2pdf fails as shown above, and a plain R CMD check reports a WARNING and an ERROR for the PDF manual. The Rd files themselves are checked by checkRd() and by the other steps of the check without TeX, so --no-manual loses only the PDF.

  • A hand-written man directory and roxygen2 together. A page of the same name that roxygen2 would write is skipped, and nothing says that the roxygen2 block above the function is then not documentation: read the "Skipping" line.

Version notes

The tables list changes that affect what this page teaches. The R entries come from the NEWS files of the corresponding releases (R NEWS) and the manual Writing R Extensions; the roxygen2 entries from its changelog (roxygen2 package documentation: Changelog), which was read on 2026-10-21.

Version Change

R 3.6.0

news() reads NEWS.md (it needs the commonmark and xml2 packages).

R 4.0.0

R CMD check --as-cran runs the \donttest examples instead of telling the tester to run them; _R_CHECK_DONTTEST_EXAMPLES_ switches that off.

R 4.1.0

\link[pkg]{foo} and \link[pkg:bar]{foo} link to topics. Before, they were interpreted as links to the files foo.html and bar.html.

R 4.2.0

Help pages typeset \eqn and \deqn with KaTeX or MathJax in HTML.

R 4.3.0

R CMD check checks .Rd files more (invalid email addresses and some invalid URIs, empty \item labels in description lists), reports problems reading NEWS.md, and optionally (included in --as-cran) checks that KaTeX renders the math of the Rd files; tools::buildVignettes() has an argument skip that R CMD check uses for vignettes whose \VignetteDepends packages are unavailable.

R 4.4.0

The Rd macro \dontdiff{} marks example code whose output is ignored when comparing check output with a reference; tools::checkRd() reports titles and section names that end in a period (ignored by R CMD check unless _R_CHECK_RD_CHECKRD_MINLEVEL_ is -5 or smaller); R CMD check notes Rd files without an \alias.

R 4.5.0

\link[=dest]{...} accepts markup in the link text; citation() results generated from package metadata include the DOIs of CRAN and Bioconductor packages; R CMD Rd2pdf makes sure that the Rd.sty of the running R is used.

R 4.6.0

Bibliographic citations and references can be generated in Rd files from bibentries (\bibcitet, \bibcitep, \bibshow, \bibinfo, evaluated at the build stage); new macros \manual{name}{node} and \linkS4methods{}; plain-text help renders \describe lists with line breaks after the labels (tools::Rd2txt_options(descStyle = NULL) restores the old look); error messages of a failed \Sexpr include the call of the original condition and warnings include Rd source locations.

Source: R NEWS: Changes in R 4.0.0 to 4.6.1

The R 3.6.0 entry is in the R 3.x NEWS (R NEWS: Changes in R 3.x). The R-devel NEWS (the upcoming 4.7.0, never run here) says at the time of writing that tools::Rd2txt() will replace --- and -- by Unicode dashes when the output encoding is UTF-8, that tools::texi2pdf() will report BibTeX warnings (so that R CMD check notes missing references when it rebuilds PDF vignettes), and that R CMD build will exclude an obsolete data/datalist file when the package uses LazyData.

roxygen2 Change

5.0.0

"_PACKAGE" documents a package.

7.0.0

@returns as an alias of @return; documentation of R6 classes; @includeRmd and @order; Markdown headings and tables; the removal of @S3method (deprecated since 4.0.0, 2014).

7.1.2

@examplesIf for conditional examples.

7.3.0

The NAMESPACE roclet reports S3 methods without @export; @describeIn suggests @rdname.

7.3.3

Custom @family titles support Markdown; @examplesIf uses withAutoprint().

8.0.0 (2026-05-01)

Requires R 4.1; options in Config/roxygen2/ fields and the version in Config/roxygen2/version (migrated automatically); needs_roxygenize(); support for S7 (@prop); more documentation inherited by R6 classes, @R6method; one-line tags warn when they span several lines; documenting a plain value no longer adds \docType{data}; the rd-other article is split into rd-datasets, rd-packages, rd-S3, rd-S4 and rd-R6.

8.1.0 (2026-08-04)

Flags in Config/roxygen2/ are case-insensitive; the migration of the version field happens whenever needed; multi-line @importFrom accepted again, as one directive per package; setAs() and setGroupGeneric() recognised; link targets resolved with cached indexes (the rdtools package).

8.1.1 (2026-10-08)

:= recognised as assignment (S7); S7 method usage wrapped in \special{}; non-syntactic names in @importFrom are double-quoted; fixes to @inherit and @inheritParams.

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Changelog

Other tools: devtools 2.5.0 deprecated devtools::build_vignettes() (the message the script printed); pkgdown 2.2.1 (the version here) warns that Bootstrap 3 is deprecated and builds an llms.txt file among the pages of the site; usethis 3.2.2 writes Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) in DESCRIPTION when markdown is turned on, which roxygen2 8 still reads; S7 is 0.2.2, and its roxygen2 support is in its first release; the Quarto command-line program is 1.10.19.
